title: PTSD Radio
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: A horror anthology of short, loosely linked vignettes, many under five pages, connected by Ogushi-sama, a sinister god tied to hair whose idol brings uncanny bodily horrors on townspeople who neglect it. Interstitial narration links the 'frequencies', and later volumes add first-person 'True Stories' about the author's own experiences (Kodansha blurb via AniList/MU; The Comics Journal).
life_message: Dread can fall on anyone at random, and the world will not notice; the series offers atmosphere, not a lesson.

content.note: Uncanny bodily harm more than fighting (TCJ); AniList Body Horror (to verify gore level).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: No honor contests; victims are passive (TCJ).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Rules of tribute must be kept or harm follows (TCJ).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Rural, local community bound by shared custom (AniList Rural).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: No clear hierarchy beyond the god.

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Folk god, offerings and hair symbolism drive the stories (Kodansha blurb).

folkways.japan: A local deity demanding tribute and hair as an offering or penance draw on Japanese folk-religious practice and the kaidan ghost-story tradition.

delivery.evidence: The Comics Journal finds no explicit moral; only ominous narration and an indifferent world.
delivery.note: The anthology offers mood and dread rather than an argued message.

winners_losers: No one wins; ordinary townspeople suffer at random. The worldview given weight is an indifferent, unknowable universe.
